name: The lord's lands
offers: Grain for coin in a good year, a market for wool and hides, the law when it is called.
threatens: Taxes taken early, the tithe barn emptied, a feast commanded when the stores are thin, the lord's son and his temper.

name: The next valley
offers: A buyer for what the valley has spare, salt and iron by the pack train, word of the wider world.
threatens: A failed harvest there means they come to buy, or to take, grain here; sickness travels with their peddlers.

name: The forest road
offers: Game, wood, and the only way west; a hunter who knows it eats well.
threatens: Wolves in daylight when the deep woods fail, bandits at dusk, deserters hiding armed, a road nobody watches after dark.

name: The market town
offers: Tools, herbs, wine and news for coin or grain; a traveling merchant now and then; a forge.
threatens: Prices that insult everyone, a foul well, thieves in the crowd, and rumor that reaches the castle before the truth does.
